column1: # kinds      verse: the source's verse (markup and all) is read as after; letters: the word's letters before become after; prepend/append: the words of after open/close the verse; drop: the word reading before goes; block: the verses own and before are one block the source stores under each number, kept once at own stating them all; divide: the word opens the verse after (the source prints no number there)
# PolGdanska 1.0 numbers 70 chapters as the Hebrew does but stores them in SWORD's King James slots: a psalm's title is
# its verse 1, and the verses beyond the King James count stand inside the chapter's last verse. Each row below divides
# such a last verse where the next Hebrew verse begins, so the text holds the Hebrew's verses and the frame places them
# (versification original): measured against UBG2018, 70 chapters read a verse off before and 6 after. Left as they are:
# Psalm 14 (its title numbered apart, which the Hebrew does not), Job 40-41 (nine Hebrew verses run into 40:24), Haggai 2
# (numbered as the Latin is), and 1 Samuel 15, Ezra 2 and Job 37, where the module runs two verses into one.
